result.title: Nobel Prize for Economics & Gold's Surging Value | WEF | Stories of the Week
result.description:
This week's top stories of the week include:

00:14 - Gold has been surging in value. Why?:
The price of gold rose by 64% in 2025, reaching an all-time high in January 2026. James Emmett, CEO of precious metals company MKS PAMP, says the key driver is uncertainty. Amid geopolitical and financial instability, central banks seek to boost their reserves of gold to protect against shocks.

01:58 - These economists won the Nobel prize for transforming policy-making:
The work of this year’s winners of the Nobel Prize for Economics has made central banks and governments ‘better equipped to deal with shocks in the economy’, says the committee chair.New Nobel laureates Robert E. Hall and Michael Woodford showed how economies are shaped by the decisions taken by individual households and businesses - and how those decisions, in turn, are shaped by people’s expectations of the future.

03:17 - This woman’s daughter was burned by a cooking stove. So she created a safer stove for everyone:
When Charlot Magayi’s daughter was two, she suffered severe burns on an open cooking stove. The tragedy inspired Magayi to create Mukuru Clean Stoves, which solve three key problems: cooking safety, indoor air #pollution and the cost of fuel. Here, she talks us through the inspiration and effort behind her game-changing innovation.

06:43 - ‘Sport is the great unifier’ Grenada’s first-ever Olympic medallist on the power of sport in life:
At the 2012 Olympics, Kirani James made history by winning Grenada’s first-ever Olympic gold medal. Since then, the 400-metre runner has faced good times and tough ones, such as when he was diagnosed with Graves’ disease. Here, he explains how the lessons he’s learned in #sport have benefited him in life, and why sport can be a route to values, well-being and community cohesion.

result.title: The critical minerals race isn’t just about mining
result.description:
The race for critical minerals is entering a new phase. As demand surges from AI, electrification and the wider energy transition, securing supplies of these vital materials is not simply a question of finding and extracting new sources - it's about processing, too, and the supply chains that connect them.

As rising geopolitical tensions expose the vulnerabilities of this system, Yun B. Choi, CEO and Executive Chairman of Korea Zinc, explains why building resilient, diversified processing capacity is becoming a strategic priority.

The World Economic Forum's Securing Minerals for Energy and Technologies aims to strengthen resilience, promote responsible development and mobilize finance for global mineral value chains. Learn more: https://initiatives.weforum.org/securing-minerals-energy-technologies/home

result.title: Betazone: Sensing the Invisible
result.description:
The world around us is filled with signals we cannot hear, see or feel, from wireless activity in a room to biological signals beneath our skin and information moving through the ocean. New forms of sensing are beginning to make this hidden world visible.

What becomes possible when we can sense the world in entirely new ways?

Join engineer and scientist Fadel Adib for a visual journey into the emerging world of wireless sensing, exploring how new technologies can change how we understand and interact with the world, and the applications of these technologies across health, climate, retail, commerce, robotics, and more.
 
Speakers: Fadel Adib

result.title: Reading the Youth Pulse
result.description:
We keep asking young people what they want. The sharper question is what they already understand that the rest of us have yet to grasp. Drawing on the World Economic Forum’s Youth Pulse report, which captures the perspectives of nearly 10,000 young people across regions, this discussion explores the signals emerging from a generation growing up amid rapid change. 

What might today’s leaders need to unlearn to keep pace with the generation already adapting to what comes next?
 
Speakers: AbdelQader AlSaqqaf, Tiffany Lee, Kacha (Shogun) Mahadumrongkul, Khalid Mohammed Al Nuaimi, Sakshi Sharma
